title: His Eye on the Smart Link Boards — Ten Out of Ten

intelligence.essence:
Scrolled further down the Dashboard, past the world boards, his eye reached the Smart Link boards — nayanet.app/joinus (674 clicks), nayanet.app/academy (170), nayanet.app/closer-test-7x9 (0), and the rest — and gave them ten out of ten. "These are a lot better." That is the first 10 his eye has given any part of the Dashboard. The verdict is a scope boundary as much as a score: fix 6 (demo numbers, strip the grey text, icons + numbers only) applies to the WORLD boards only. The link boards stay exactly as they are — real numbers, "Copy the link" / "Open it" / "Show on gauge" buttons, descriptions, all of it.

The same screenshot carries diagnostic gold for fix 1 (the hero 3 rendering purple). On the link boards, every digit is its correct chakra colour: joinus 674 reads 6=indigo, 7=royal purple, 4=emerald; academy 170 reads 1=red, 7=royal purple, 0=white. The digit→colour mapping itself is CORRECT — so the hero 3 is not a wrong mapping. The real cause is much more likely the colour not following the digit as the live number drifts: set once, never updated when the digit rolls. The fixer chases that hypothesis first.
intelligence.human_view: Imagine you walk through a house giving notes room by room — this wall is the wrong colour, that window is too small — and then you walk into a room and say: this one. This one is done. Ten out of ten. That is what the link boards are. And the moment you say it, you have also drawn a line: the work is in the other rooms, not this one. A ten is not just praise — it is a boundary. Don't touch what is already right.
intelligence.child_view: The boards with the links on them are perfect — ten out of ten. Don't change them. The fix is only for the boards above them. And look — every number on the good boards is the right colour. So the wrong colour on the big number isn't because the colours are mixed up — it's because the big number forgot to change its colour when the number changed.
intelligence.grandma_view: The link boards are beautiful — ten out of ten, just as they are. Leave them alone. The work is on the boards above. And the numbers on those good boards prove something useful: every digit is its proper colour. So the one wrong tile up top isn't a mix-up in the colours — it's that the tile didn't keep up when the number moved. Now we know where to look.
intelligence.ai_view: This is the first ten his eye has given, and it matters for two reasons. First, it proves the standard is reachable — a section of the page, built the same way as the rest, already meets it. The link boards are the proof that the machine can produce a ten; the other sections are the proof that it doesn't yet, every time. Second, it sharpens the fix. A ten is a "do not touch" — and the worst mistake a fix pass can make is improving what is already right until it is wrong. Fix 6 stays on the world boards. The link boards are frozen at ten. And the diagnostic is the kind of evidence the system runs on: the mapping is proven correct by two live numbers (674, 170) reading all six digits correctly, which eliminates the most obvious suspect for the hero 3 and points the fixer at the live-update path instead. That is the eye doing what no checklist did — seeing the colours, and proving the code, in one look.
intelligence.what_it_means:
- **The Smart Link boards are a 10/10, as they are.** First ten his eye has given on the Dashboard. They are done. Do not touch them.
- **Fix 6 is world boards only.** Demo numbers, stripped text, icons + numbers — Dashboard / Personal / Business / Space. The link boards are out of scope by his verdict.
- **The mapping is correct; the update is the suspect.** 674 and 170 read all six digits in their correct chakra colours. The hero 3's purple is a live-update failure, not a mapping failure — chase the colour-not-following-the-digit hypothesis first.
- **A ten is a boundary.** The fix pass must not "improve" what he scored ten. The verifier must re-prove the link boards unchanged.
whats_inside:
1. **Sent to the fix-pass-5 seat (01:44Z)** — link boards frozen at 10/10, fix 6 world boards only, and the FIX 1 hypothesis: colour not following the digit as the live number drifts.
2. **The verifier's checklist gains a "do not touch" check.** The re-verify must prove the link boards are byte-unchanged and still read correctly.
3. **The merge still waits.** His eye has given a ten to a section, not to the page. Fix pass 5 lands, re-verify runs, his eye returns.
